 Order

The short grievance of the petitioner who has lost the land under the provisions of National Highways Act, 1956 is against the long pendency of the matter at the hands of the respondent who happens to be the statutory Arbitrator u/s.3G(5) & (6) of the Highways Act, 1956.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that right to property being constitutionally guaranteed under Article 300A; the acquisition of property for being valid needs payment of compensation and where the grievance is as to the quantum of compensation paid, the statutory Arbitrator cannot keep the matter pending indefinitely.
He also says that right to speedy justice avails to his client.
3. Learned AGA appearing for the Respondent opposes the petition contending that the petition lacks material particulars and therefore no relief can be granted to the petitioner.

He also highlights the enormity fo work which the Deputy Commissioners shoulder int eh district administration and contens that, no mandamus can be NC: 2023:KHC:20638 issued to such an officer to decide the matter within a particular period.

4. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and having perused the petition papers, this court is broadly in agreement with the submission of learned counsel for the petitioner that the arbitration proceedings at the hands of the statutory Arbitrator cannot be kept in cold storage indefinitely; atleast as a concession to the shortness of human life, the respondent Arbitrator has to arbitrate the dispute and pass order within an outer limit of three months.
All contentions are to be kept open.
Writ petition is accordingly disposed off.
If delay is brooked, it is open to the petitioner to move an appropriate application before the Court seeking levy of heavy costs on the Arbitrator payable by him.

Sd/-
